Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — A solid thermal day with clear skies, a sharp lapse rate, and no precipitation. Peak thermal strength is moderate to strong (up to 506 ft/min), but afternoon westerly winds increase significantly at ridge-top sites, making morning and early afternoon the preferred window for most launches.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury Grade: Marginal — Winds turn strong westerly (20–26 mph) from 2pm onward, exceeding the preferred SE component; favorable window 9am–1pm, peak w* 389 ft/min, thermal ceiling ~4,531 ft AGL. Caution: sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.1 °C/km).
  • Hallelujah: Favorable — Light morning winds and good thermal alignment; westerly flow builds to 15–16 mph by mid-afternoon but remains within preferred range. Best window 10am–5pm, peak w* 450 ft/min, thermal ceiling ~5,218 ft AGL. Caution: sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.7 °C/km).
  • Slide Mountain: Marginal — Persistent west winds (15–21 mph) are cross to the preferred SE launch, though thermals develop early. Flyable 9am–3pm, peak w* 318 ft/min, thermal ceiling ~2,012 ft AGL. Caution: sharp thermals (lapse rate 8.7 °C/km).
  • McClellan: Favorable — Light drainage flow transitions to manageable SW-W winds; best thermal window 12:30pm–4pm, peak w* 499 ft/min, thermal ceiling ~5,333 ft AGL. Caution: sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.7 °C/km).
  • West McClellan: Favorable — Winds align with preferred W-NW launch, though speeds pick up to 18 mph with gusts to 24 mph in the afternoon. Best window 11am–4pm, peak w* 395 ft/min, thermal ceiling ~3,598 ft AGL. Caution: sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.1 °C/km).
  • Peavine Mountain: Marginal — Strong SW flow (18–25 mph) all day is cross to the preferred southerly launch, creating challenging ridge soaring; sled-run thermals possible. Window 9:30am–2pm, peak w* 420 ft/min, thermal ceiling ~4,057 ft AGL. Caution: sharp thermals (lapse rate 8.5 °C/km).
  • Rainbow Ridge: Favorable — Light morning winds clock around to westerly 13–15 mph in the afternoon; best thermals mid-day. Window 9:30am–4pm, peak w* 506 ft/min, thermal ceiling ~6,787 ft AGL. Caution: sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.9 °C/km) — advanced pilots only.
  • Duck Hill: Favorable — Afternoon westerly flow (15–20 mph) is on-and-off cross but ridge-soarable; strong late-day push. Window 11am–3pm, peak w* 483 ft/min, thermal ceiling ~6,617 ft AGL. Caution: sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.5 °C/km).
  • Daydreams: Marginal — Weak, inconsistent thermals (peak w* only 146 ft/min) and gusty afternoon SW winds (16 mph) limit soaring potential. Best window 8am–10am or late evening, peak thermal ceiling ~3,718 ft AGL. Caution: sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.3 °C/km).

Hazards

  • Sharp thermals — Lapse rates of 8.5–9.9 °C/km at all sites; strong, punchy lift suitable for advanced/expert pilots only.
  • Moderate low-level shear — Peak layer speed shear reaches 5–7 mph at McClellan, West McClellan, Kingsbury, Rainbow Ridge, Duck Hill, and Slide Mountain; could affect low-altitude handling.
  • Afternoon wind increase — Westerly gusts up to 26 mph at exposed ridge sites (Kingsbury, Peavine, Duck Hill) after 2pm; higher turbulence and challenging landings possible.
  • Rotor/lee turbulence potential — Downwind of Peavine Mountain and Carson Range ridgelines as westerly flow strengthens in the afternoon.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
Wind thresholds: orange = 12 mph, red = 18 mph.
